title: Multimodal EEG and fNIRS Biosignal Acquisition during Motor Imagery Tasks in Patients with Orthopedic Impairment
description: This dataset comprises simultaneous 18-channel EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings from 7 participants with orthopedic impairment during motor imagery tasks. Participants performed four different motor imagery conditions (reach, twist, lift, grasp) across three sessions with 40 trials each, following a standardized paradigm with visual cueing and fixation periods. The multimodal biosignal acquisition provides complementary hemodynamic and electrophysiological measures of motor imagery processing in a clinical population.
methods_description: EEG and fNIRS data were acquired simultaneously during motor imagery tasks. Each trial consisted of a 3-second fixation cross, followed by a 4-second visual cue, a 3-second ready state with gray screen, and a 5-second motor imagery execution period. Four motor imagery tasks (reach, twist, lift, grasp) were presented in random order across 40 trials per session over three sessions.
